bug_semantics: NLTK corpus readers IPIPANCorpusReader, CrubadanCorpusReader, and LinThesaurusCorpusReader take in-root paths from trusted corpus state (CorpusReader.abspaths()/root joins, or FileSystemPathPointer.replace('morph.xml','header.xml') which returns a plain str because FileSystemPathPointer subclasses str) and reopen those paths with builtins.open() instead of nltk.pathsec.open()/PathPointer.open(). Under pathsec.ENFORCE=True a symlink planted inside an allowlisted corpus root as header.xml, table.txt, <code>-3grams.txt, or simN.lsp is followed by builtins.open() and outside-root content is returned through public methods channels(), domains(), categories(), langs(), crubadan_to_iso(), synonyms(), and scored_synonyms(), while pathsec.open() of the same targets is blocked (CWE-22/CWE-59). First-party GHSA-p4rw-rvv2-7xwr reproduced this on 3.9.4 and v3.10.0-rc2; CVE-2026-79676 (PUBLISHED) and the vendor advisory mark <=3.10.2 affected and >=3.10.3 patched.
flaw_origin: The leftover builtins.open() of root-derived corpus files was first written when IPIPANCorpusReader was added: a2167eb7a17fe51842bdee1c9c93cf5b7da14614 (2009-07-19) introduced nltk/corpus/reader/ipipan.py _get_tag with `header = open(f, 'r').read()` after abspath().replace('morph.xml','header.xml'). The same mechanism was later written independently in LinThesaurusCorpusReader (2eabeab4114c047649175487d8c97bc2d7f16b69, 2012-03-28, `with open(path) as lin_file` over abspaths() PathPointers) and CrubadanCorpusReader (4e3f9cc11d8a53fea37e47a1aba021b875352969 as langid.py, 2015-01-23, `open(mapper_file,'rU')` / `open(ngram_file,'rU')`; rename-only 909ce29373a9e1771c388c1e253f9d169a63019f is not a BIC). Pyupgrade/context-manager commits restyled those calls without changing the sink. Pathsec 4386e344d94c5bd0071ee52732638f6929d59d8a (2026-03-17) shadowed open() in nltk/data.py so PathPointer.open() became sandboxed, but it did not convert these reader-local builtins.open() sites; that incomplete control is how the pre-existing lines became a trusted-root bypass, not a first-write of them.
